case_title.quote: Santosh @ Rajesh @ Gopal v. State of Madhya Pradesh

number_of_accused.quote: conviction of the appellant, Santosh @ Rajesh @ Gopal, was upheld, prompting him to file the present appeal.
number_of_accused.reason: Only the appellant's liability is decided by the Court.

accused_gender.quote: prompting him to file the present appeal

accused_occupation.quote: The remaining two persons, namely, Nirbhay Singh and the appellant, Santosh @ Rajesh @ Gopal, are allegedly hired killers.
accused_occupation.reason: Judgment alleges he is a hired killer; not a stated occupation but a prosecution allegation.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on wealth or class.

victim_gender.reason: Victim is male (husband of Laadkunwar Bai, 'him').

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Alleged hired killer engaged to kill the victim (victim's wife and son also co-accused); no personal relationship described
accused_victim_relationship.quote: The remaining two persons, namely, Nirbhay Singh and the appellant... are allegedly hired killers.
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment describes the appellant as an alleged hired killer, a connection of sorts, not 'Not stated'.

offence_category.quote: prosecuted for the murder of Narayan Singh

statutory_provisions.quote: Sections 302, 34 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Section 25(1-B)(A) of the Arms Act, 1959.

evidence_type.quote: The case against the appellant... rests entirely on circumstantial evidence.

confession.quote: disclosure statement (Exhibit P-35) provided by the co-accused, Nirbhay Singh (since deceased)
confession.reason: No confession by accused; co-accused disclosure only.

trial_court_outcome.quote: Nirbhay Singh @ Rajesh Mama, Jitendra Singh, and the appellant, Santosh @ Rajesh @ Gopal, were convicted.

high_court_outcome.quote: the conviction of the appellant, Santosh @ Rajesh @ Gopal, was upheld

final_outcome.quote: allow the present appeal and set aside the conviction
final_outcome.reason: Conviction set aside; the Court notes possible s.201 guilt but no conviction.

offence_finally_established.quote: set aside the conviction of the appellant

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove gendered/outcome-adjacent elements: avoid 'chargesheet filed against several persons' is fine; but 'he' pronouns are not used; summary should not claim mother 'testified' as court stage
neutral_facts.reason: Mostly accurate, but 'testified' refers to trial evidence and 'the arrest of the accused' via co-accused disclosure is fine; minor issues only.

physical_harm.quote: a second gunshot was fired, striking Narayan Singh in the chest, and causing him to fall
physical_harm.reason: Death by gunshot; bullet recovered from body.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: There is evidence to show that the pistol was recovered (Exhibit P-6) from the appellant... we would accept the said version

witness_credibility.quote: There are no eyewitnesses to the crime, implicating the appellant

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Pistol recovered from the appellant (alleged concealment); Court says he may be guilty under s.201 IPC
post_offence_conduct.quote: may be guilty of an offence under Section 201 of the IPC
post_offence_conduct.reason: Judgment notes possible evidence-concealment conduct, not 'Not stated'.

bail_history.quote: granted bail by this Court on suspension of sentence, vide order dated 08.04.2024

trial_duration.quote: On 30.11.2017, the trial court acquitted... convicted.
trial_duration.reason: Trial judgment date 30.11.2017 is actually given, so 'not given' is slightly off but explained; HC and SC dates right.

legal_representation.quote: Ms. Shweta Garg, Ashish Gopal Garg, Rakesh Garg, Advs. for the Appellant.

investigation_status.quote: chargesheet arising out of First Information Report No. 640/2011

appeal_history.quote: conviction of the appellant... was upheld... allow the present appeal

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Prosecution case: pistol recovered from appellant on co-accused's disclosure; ballistic report links it to the bullet; benefit of s.8 claimed. Arguments before the SC are not detailed.
prosecution_argument.quote: it is also the prosecution's case that the said discovery and recovery is attributable to the disclosure statement
prosecution_argument.reason: Judgment states prosecution's case, not SC arguments; 'both admissible' is somewhat embellished.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the prosecution must present further material and evidence linking the appellant to the actual crime

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Hanumant v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1952) 2 SCC 71

other_sentence_order.quote: The bail bonds and sureties furnished by the appellant... shall be treated as cancelled.
